resources.string: A tiny Discord bot that runs on your phone
Get one at discord.com/developers → your app → Bot → Reset Token
/roblox looks up Roblox users, avatars, games and groups using the public Roblox API.
Quick add: a name and some text. For scripts and a function palette use the bot builder.
%1$d saved · %2$d allowed with the built-ins you have on
What Discord shows under the bot name: activity type, the main line, an optional second line, a stream URL for Streaming, and whether the bot appears online, idle, do not disturb or invisible.
Activity line, e.g. with slash commands

Discord lets bots set only the activity name, state, type and URL, so images, buttons and party info are not offered here — the API would ignore them. Rich presence with artwork needs the Discord Social SDK, a native library for C++/Unity/Unreal, not a plain Java app.
Activity type, two text lines, stream URL and online status.
What it replies with. {user} mentions the caller
None yet. Build one below, or use /custom add in Discord.
Turn built-in commands on or off. Discord allows 100 commands per server, shared with your custom ones.
Off commands are not registered in Discord and make room for custom commands. The newer commands (server tools, warnings, text tools) start switched off — pick the ones you want.
Build commands the way Bot Designer for Discord does: pick functions, drop them into a script, test it on the phone and save. Responses are real Discord replies — nothing here is simulated.
Write a command with $functions: $mention, $args, $if, variables and more. Preview it, then save it.
No commands yet. Write one above and press Save.
Bring the bot back automatically when the phone restarts. The phone still has to be on: an app cannot stay online with the device powered off.
